Start.Title: Create a Character
Start.IntroHint: The wizard walks through {count} steps. You can move back and forth with the buttons below — nothing is saved until you press Create Character on the last step.
Start.Flow2: Race — costs BP and grants attribute modifiers.
Start.Flow4: Age — modifies attributes and starting capital (placed early, before the steps that read it — a deliberate deviation from the book's page order, see code comment).
Start.Flow6: Profession — requires certain attribute values, so they're bought first.
Start.Flow8: Special abilities — rolled, costs BP (after profession, BEFORE you spend EP on skills — so you know if an ability already grants bonus FV to something before buying it yourself).
Start.Flow9: Social standing and starting capital — rolled, costs BP.
Start.Flow10: Languages — mother tongue is granted by race and social standing (RP p.42/44), no roll.
Start.Flow11: Profession skills and skills — choose skills from the profession's list (RP p.11), then base chances + buy with EP (same book section, RP p.30, a step right after the previous one here).
Start.Flow12: Life goal and equipment — shop with the starting capital.
Start.Flow13: Review — check everything and create the character.
Start.Note1: Gender, race, and profession can't be changed later. They control attribute modifiers, portrait, and profession skills, and changing them afterward would retroactively recalculate things the character has already used in play. Choose them carefully.
Start.Note2: Everything else — abilities, skills, age, life goal — can be unlocked for editing by the GM afterward: the GM clicks the padlock at the top of the character sheet, which reveals an Edit in Wizard button. The equipment step is skipped then; purchases after character creation happen through a merchant.
Start.EditModeHint: You are in edit mode on an existing character. Race and profession are shown but locked, and the equipment step is skipped.

Kon.Hint: Choose gender. Controls which portrait images are shown for race and profession in the next step.

Niva.Hint: Choose the character's tier (Hjältarnas Handbok p.37-39). All tiers share the same base of 125 BP (HH p.6) — but the hero tiers ADDITIONALLY get to roll heroic deeds for bonus BP and extra HP on top of the base.
Niva.EpByAgeHint: Experience points at creation depend on BOTH tier and age (HH p.8) — age is chosen in a later step, but tier alone already determines which of these rows you'll land on:
Niva.HjaltedadHint: Heroic deeds (HH p.6-7) grant bonus BP and hero points (a separate currency, not hit points) on top of the regular pool — a two-step process: first {formula} to decide HOW MANY times you get to roll, then that many 1d20 rolls against the table.
Niva.HouseRuleWarning: ⚠ House rule (non-standard) — see the GM settings.
Niva.RollCountResult: {formula} gave {count} — you get to roll {count} times on the heroic-deeds table.
Niva.RollResultsSummary: {count} rolls — total +{bp} BP, +{points} hero points. Saved automatically as special abilities on the character sheet.
Niva.ResultNote: {notes} — not applied automatically, see the note on the character.

Ras.EditHint: Race can't be changed in edit mode — it defines the character and drives racial bonuses via ActiveEffects. If it must be changed anyway: have the GM drag a new race onto the sheet.
Ras.ChooseHint: Choose a race. Automatic abilities and attribute modifiers are shown below.

Alder.AgeModHint: Age modifiers to attributes are applied (RP p.24-25): Young STY-1/STO-1/SMI+1/PSY+1, Old STY-2/STO-1/INT+1/PSY+2/SMI-1. The EP budget is spent in the next step, on skills.

Attribut.Hint: Buy your attributes with BP (RP p.23) — the starting value 3 (STO: {raceName}'s normal value) costs nothing, every step above costs more. The race's modifier is applied automatically and shown immediately. Spent on attributes so far: {total} BP.
Attribut.NextGroupUpPrefix: The next point raises the group to

Attribut.QualifiedHint: {qualified} of {total} professions have their attribute requirements met with these values.

Formagor.Hint: Special abilities (RP p.25-27). Number of rows ({slots}) is set by tier (KH p.3). Enter how much BP you want to spend (min 1, max 40) and press "Roll" to roll 2d20+BP against the table — the fields fill in automatically but can be edited by hand afterward.

Yrke.EditHint: Profession can't be changed in edit mode — it controls which profession skills the character has. If it must be changed anyway: have the GM drag a new profession onto the sheet.
Yrke.ChooseHint: Choose a profession. Every profession has attribute requirements (RP p.11) — shown on the cards and colored by whether your purchased values meet them. An unmet requirement doesn't block the choice: check with the GM.
Yrke.NoQualifyTitle: No profession requirements are met. With the attributes purchased, the character doesn't qualify for any of the {count} professions — the lowest requirement in the whole list is 12.
Yrke.NoQualifyBody: Go back and adjust your purchases, or choose a profession anyway and check with the GM.
Yrke.QualifiedHint: {qualified} of {total} professions have their requirements met.
Yrke.ReqUnmetTitle: The requirements aren't met — can still be chosen, but check with the GM

Magiskola.Hint: Choose the spellcaster's main school (MAG p.8-10). A magic school is, mechanically, a skill value — the school is created as a skill, and you raise its FV with EP in the skills step just like other profession skills. FV in the school determines which spells you can learn and the highest effect grade you can manage.

Yrkesfardigheter.ChooseHint: Choose {target} profession skills from {profession}'s list (RP p.11{magicNote}). Other skills on the list can be learned as secondary skills later, but cost more EP.
Yrkesfardigheter.WeaponCountHint: The number of weapon choices is set by the profession's own list (RP p.11) and varies a lot: combat-focused professions and warrior specializations choose among several weapon types, while professions with a different focus (magic, crafting, social skills, etc.) usually choose only a few — or, as here, just one.

Hand.Hint: The hand you normally use is called your sword hand; the off hand is called your shield hand. The shield hand is consistently worse — except for the skills Two Weapons and Shield (RP p.27).
Hand.GrantedQuestion: Did you get the hand as a special ability? Then you don't roll.
Hand.BpLabel: BP to spend on sword hand
Hand.Tip: 2d6+15 is at least 17 — so at least Ambidextrous-with-training is guaranteed, and Fully ambidextrous in 92% of cases. Buying off your worse hand early saves a lot later — and Fully ambidextrous also lets you fight with two known weapons in any combination immediately, without first training your own Two Weapons skill for that pair.
Hand.NoOffHandPerk: No worse hand — the shield hand's −10 CL doesn't apply to you.
Hand.AmbidextriosPerk: You can also fight with two known weapons in any combination without training a Two Weapons skill first — as long as the combination is reasonable (no two-handed weapons, not bow+sword). An ambidextrous-with-training character still has to train each weapon combination separately (RP p.59).
Hand.TableDubbelhantNote: — both hands equally good, but not at the same time
Hand.TableAmbidextriosNote: — both hands at once, on different things

Socialt.Hint: Roll for social standing. Every BP spent gives +1 on the roll (RP p.27).

Kapital.MultiplierNote: The age multiplier is applied in the Age step — see PLAN_WIZARD_V2.md Phase 4.

Sprak.Hint: Mother tongue is granted by race and social standing (RP p.42/44) — no roll, just a choice where race offers several options. Speaking and Reading/Writing count as SEPARATE skills with their own base chances (BC); some races (dwarves, half-orcs, half-elves) speak more languages than they can read/write.
Sprak.IncompleteWarning: ⚠ All language choices must be filled in before you can continue.
Sprak.ReferenceSummary: The languages of Ereb Altor (reference — Campaign Book p.44)

Fardigheter.Hint: Base skill value (FV) = base chance (BC, group of the attribute — REGLER_EGENSKAPER.md). Raise FV with EP below — RP p.30: the cost increases per step (cumulative table), and depends on the skill's category (primary 2 / profession skill 3 / secondary 5 EP per base step). The button greys out when EP isn't enough or the max starting FV ({maxFv}, KH p.3) is reached.
Fardigheter.NoStructuredSkillsHint: No structured profession skills for {profession} yet — see item-yrke.mjs's research gap. Add manually via the sheet's "New skill" button after creation.

Utrustning.Hint: Buy equipment with the starting capital. Cards grey out when the price exceeds remaining capital. Cards with one field and a unit (e.g. "sm/g") are bought in QUANTITY — enter how many grams/doses/kegs you want, the total price is calculated automatically. Cards marked "Reference" have no price of their own at all (they price a DIFFERENT item, e.g. an untamed mount) and can't be bought here.
